report:
The three sisters agree on a first set of steps. Nothing has been decided about the house, and that is on purpose.

The shared list of needs, concerns and expectations, which all three have seen:
1. A wants to make the house a home with her husband. She wants a price that feels fair to B and C, and she will not go ahead without C's agreement. She cannot say whether she can afford the house until the will and the appraisal are known.
2. B wants her share to help her start a dance studio. She has no deadline right now.
3. C will consider a sale to A only at a price that gives each sister what she would get from an outside sale after actual costs. She will not accept an extra discount. She wants a say in choosing the appraiser, and she has not agreed to a sale.
4. Everyone agrees that the will, the shares, the value of the house and the sale costs must be confirmed first.
5. My own: all three see the same list, and no one is pushed into a plan.

The agreed next steps are:
1. Find out what the will says and who the executor is.
2. Get one independent appraisal, with all three sisters choosing the appraiser together.
3. Get a written estimate of what an outside sale would cost.

The idea still on the table, though not agreed, is that A buys at the appraised value minus only the costs that an outside sale would really bring. B and C would then receive their shares in cash.

The main open problem is that no one knows who has the will or who drafted it. A has offered to contact the executor once someone knows who that is. Good places to look are their father's papers, his former lawyer or bank, and the local probate court.

Once the will's terms and the appraisal are known, the next task is to see whether A can afford the house on that basis. If she cannot, the sisters can compare this plan with a sale to an outside buyer.

I have not made any legal or money decisions.
